clue.text: Democratic leader, national leader once

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here the first of Democratic

parts.note: a national is a citizen of a country, here a citizen of Israel

explanation.surface: A political profile of a Democratic party chief who was once head of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Democratic leader' looks like a US party figure, but it only supplies the opening D.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was twice British Prime Minister in the nineteenth century, a former head of government.

clue.text: "Gossip" about to enter dictionary, approved

indicators.note: to enter says one piece goes inside the dictionary's letters

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the gossip word is read backwards

parts.note: to yak is to chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: A piece of chatter gets accepted into the dictionary as a new word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns YAK into KAY, which goes into OED.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the OK to something is to sanction it, so the past tense is a synonym.

clue.text: Animals, those with a sting, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick, so those running one are swindlers who cheat

explanation.surface: A nature note about creatures that carry stings, like wasps or scorpions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sting' suggests insects, but here it is slang for a con.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest big cats of the African savannah are examples of animals.

clue.text: Vile stuff entered into problem

indicators.note: into says the entered word is placed inside the problem word

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set at school
to put data in is to enter it, so put means entered

explanation.surface: Something nasty has got into a problem someone is working on.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit and phlegm coughed up are repellent matter, fairly called vile stuff.

clue.text: Russian composer's relationship in a state

indicators.note: in says the relationship word sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation of Georgia, a US state
a link is a connection or relationship between things

explanation.surface: A Russian composer's affair, conducted while he was in a bad state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was a nineteenth-century Russian composer, father of the national school.

clue.text: Sweet drink in ancient European region, unfinished

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the shortened region name
unfinished means the region's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Gaul was the ancient Roman name for the region covering France
tea is a common drink

explanation.surface: A sweet drink taken in an old region of Europe, left half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the drink, but it is the British word for a dessert; 'unfinished' drops the final letter of the region.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich cream cake is served as a dessert, which British English calls a sweet.

clue.text: Polish composer's cold invitation to hitchhiker

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
a driver stopping for a hitchhiker says 'hop in'

explanation.surface: A Polish composer coldly offers a lift to someone thumbing by the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish-born Romantic composer and pianist.

clue.text: Figure in the negative side raised to get another

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means the letters are read bottom to top
in places the figure inside the negative side

parts.note: yin is the passive or negative principle in Chinese philosophy, opposite yang
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A number placed on the losing side is lifted up to produce a different number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like the definition, but it supplies letters; 'raised' turns the whole assembled piece upwards, and 'another' means another figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Read after 'Figure', another means a further number, and nine tens is a number.

clue.text: Sauce in salad tossed into jam

indicators.note: into says the tossed letters are placed inside the jam word

parts.note: being in a hole means being in a jam, a tight spot

indicators.note: a salad is tossed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A sauce goes into a salad that is mixed and then into some jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link: 'tossed' scrambles all seven letters of 'in salad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich emulsion of egg yolk, butter and lemon is a classic French sauce.

clue.text: Reliable and right to take into consideration

indicators.note: to take into says the consideration word has the right letter put inside it

parts.note: a study is careful consideration of something

explanation.surface: Being dependable and correct means taking everything into consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: Something robust and solid can be depended upon, so it is trustworthy.

clue.text: Subtlety, obvious one

parts.note: overt means open and obvious
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note on nuance: a subtle point versus a glaring one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets subtle against obvious, yet obvious supplies part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An implied suggestion or nuance underlying what is said is a subtlety.

clue.text: See 21
Say English composer never existed as iconic figure

indicators.note: Say tells us to speak the phrase aloud and spell what we hear

parts.note: Frederick Delius was an English composer, and something that never existed is a myth

explanation.surface: A claim that a famous English composer never really lived, though he became an icon.
explanation.walkthrough: DELIUS MYTH said aloud gives the name of Delia Smith, a famous British TV cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia Smith is a much-loved British cookery writer and broadcaster, a household icon.

clue.text: Say Austrian composer, believer with something to play

indicators.note: Say tells us to speak the names aloud and spell what we hear

parts.note: Joseph Haydn was an Austrian composer, and a Sikh is a believer in Sikhism

explanation.surface: An Austrian composer and a man of faith with something to perform together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests music to go with the composer, but it means a children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which one player hunts for the others is something to play.

clue.text: Five, moved in worship, weaken

indicators.note: moved says one letter is taken from its place and put elsewhere in the word

parts.note: to venerate is to revere or worship
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Being moved during worship leaves a person drained.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening V of VENERATE moves to after ENER.
explanation.definitionFit: To enervate is to drain of energy, so it means to make feeble.

clue.text: Mummy is admitting this compiler to bedlam (mad)

indicators.note: admitting says the scrambled letters take in the compiler's pronoun
mad signals that the letters of bedlam are in wild disorder

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so this compiler is me

explanation.surface: Mother is letting the puzzle setter into the madhouse, which is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' scrambles the letters of bedlam; 'to' is a link. A mummy is a body that is so treated, so 'Mummy is' leads to the participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptian mummies were bodies preserved with spices and resins, so a mummy is treated that way.

clue.text: German composer's English uprising dividing what divided us?

indicators.note: dividing says the upturned piece splits the conflict word in two

parts.note: a war divides nations or peoples

indicators.note: uprising in a down answer means the letters are read upwards

explanation.surface: An English rebellion breaking apart a once-divided nation, by a German composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what divided us?' is a cryptic way of describing a conflict; 'uprising' turns the abbreviation upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle of operas.

clue.text: English composer's violin part

definitions.meaning: Frank ... was an English composer, teacher of Benjamin Britten
the raised wooden support holding up a violin's strings

explanation.surface: An English composer's section for violins.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Bridge was an English composer, and the bridge is the raised support for a violin's strings.

clue.text: Say German composer sounds sheepish in part of cycle

indicators.note: Say tells us to speak the words aloud and spell what we hear

parts.note: Handel was a German-born composer, and the sounds a sheep makes are baas

explanation.surface: A German composer sounds embarrassed in part of a song cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycle' suggests a set of songs, matching the composer, but it means a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The steering bar with grips at the front of a bicycle is part of a cycle.

clue.text: Czech composer's against duck being victim of cannibalism? Not entirely

indicators.note: a duck eaten by a duck is cannibalism, so one duck goes inside the other
Not entirely says the outer duck loses its last letter

parts.note: a drake is a male duck
V is short for versus, against
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A Czech composer opposes a duck being eaten by its own kind, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' gives both O (a zero score) and DRAKE; V+O goes inside DRAK (DRAKE cut short).
explanation.definitionFit: Antonín Dvořák was a Czech composer, best known for the New World Symphony.

clue.text: Boy on one vessel or another

parts.note: Sam is a boy's name
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A boy climbs aboard one boat or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing the boy first; 'another' means another vessel, a small flat-bottomed boat used in East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed Chinese boat is a vessel, so it is another besides the pan.

clue.text: Say English composer meets American composer in walk through London

indicators.note: Say tells us the composer's name is spoken aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: William Byrd was an English Renaissance composer
John Cage was an American composer, famous for 4'33"

explanation.surface: An English composer bumps into an American one while strolling in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Birdcage Walk is a street in central London beside St James's Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdcage Walk is a London street running past St James's Park, a walk through the city.

clue.text: Has American composer passed round new book?

indicators.note: passed round says the composer's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer
VOL is short for volume, a book

explanation.surface: Has an American composer handed round a fresh book?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' is the definition, in the sense of includes; the surface reads it as the start of a question.
explanation.definitionFit: To include something as a part is to contain it, so it is a synonym of has.

clue.text: Benefit to be rejected within month, gutted, showing strain

indicators.note: within says the turned benefit word goes inside the gutted month
gutted means the month loses its insides, its middle letter

parts.note: May is a month

indicators.note: to be rejected means sent back, so the benefit word is read backwards

parts.note: the dole is state unemployment benefit in Britain

explanation.surface: Losing one's benefits within the month leaves a person gutted and under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' removes the middle letter of the month, and 'to be rejected' turns the benefit word back to front; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a tune or snatch of music, so it is a synonym for a tune.

clue.text: Retreat, retiring to a place in Venice (with 17)

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the retreat word is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den, a retreat

explanation.surface: A getaway: heading back to a spot in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: With 17 the full answer is the Rialto Bridge over the Grand Canal; 'retiring' turns LAIR into RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is a district of Venice, famous for its market and its bridge.

clue.text: French-American composer gripped by comeback of Chinese "Ravel"

indicators.note: comeback of says the hidden letters are read backwards
gripped by says the letters are held within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A French-American composer is clutched by a Chinese-made version of a Ravel piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'gripped' in the definition, but 'gripped by' is what signals the letters held inside Chinese Ravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgard Varèse was a French-born composer who worked in America.
